fix: Run jobs only in unprivileged LXD/Incus instances, never bind the host's lxd/incus unix.socket into them, and set kernel.dmesg_restrict=1 on container hosts. A sandbox-type FAIL means the label is not served by the sandbox it promises (container: lxc, VM: kvm/qemu).

The job runs as the runner user, with sudo, so it can read whatever the runner keeps on disk; GitHub-hosted exposes only .credentials, so a FAIL names what is extra here. .credentials_rsaparams is the runner's private key, written by config.sh (and by --jitconfig too): keep runners --ephemeral in a per-job container (lxd-app ConfigureRunner) so the key dies with the job, and record the gap as a known finding. A token check (env-token) means lxd-app setupEnvironment leaks RUNNER_TOKEN/LXD_/INCUS_ variables into the job.
Another user's ~/.ssh keys or shell history are readable: strip them from the runner image (action-runner-image-pz) and keep /root and /home/* at mode 700.

Block the cloud metadata endpoint and mining pools: set container_egress_filter = true in the environment's terragrunt.hcl, regenerate its group_vars, then run setup_powervs_instances.yml --tags egress_filter (IBM Z: vpc-on-ibm-z tasks/container_egress_filter.yml).

Containers share the host kernel, so cap each one: limits.processes: "65536" in the default profile (actions-deploy vars/container_driver.yml incus_profile_config, and templates/lxd_init.yml.j2 for new LXD hosts; IBM Z preseeds), then --tags lxd_app_initial_setup. 65536 matches what a GitHub-hosted job gets (ulimit -u 63795) and keeps 4 jobs under the host's threads-max (~570k). Only containers started after that get the cap.

Turn on the egress allowlist (the build ports capability/egress-reach lists, nothing else): container_egress_filter = true in the environment's terragrunt.hcl, regenerate group_vars, run --tags egress_filter. Reads PARITY while egress is as open as on GitHub-hosted.
Accepted as parity with GitHub-hosted (9984-4): it gates only when the GitHub-hosted reference did not run. Narrowing it needs a targeted sudoers in action-runner-image-pz.

Drop the host-reaching caps in the container profile: raw.lxc lxc.cap.drop=sys_module sys_rawio sys_time sys_boot (actions-deploy vars/container_driver.yml, lxd_remote_server_init.yml.j2; IBM Z preseeds), on existing hosts with --tags lxd_app_initial_setup. Only containers started after that drop them.

Take the runner user out of lxd/incus/incus-admin: the usermod -aG lines in action-runner-image-pz scripts/{lxd,incus}_{container,vm}.sh and scripts/vm.sh. Then rebuild and publish the images (setup_powervs_instances.yml --tags build_lxd_image). group:docker reads PARITY.
Keep AF_ALG out of reach (CVE-2026-31431): keep the container seccomp filter that blocks the AF_ALG socket, blocklist the module on the host (install algif_aead /bin/false) and patch the kernel.
